intro: We are on Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan, the first day of the new month. In the biblical calendar, the new moon was announced by the blowing of trumpets and marked with special offerings. This day, 30 Tishrei, begins the month of Cheshvan — sometimes called Marcheshvan, meaning “bitter Cheshvan,” because it is the only month with no festivals. The joy of Tishrei is past; the work of the year begins.
